collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HONESTY AND ACCOUNTABILITY (HON-01 to HON-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Small lies, kind fibs, things left unsaid, things forgotten, honest mistakes and the odd careless one. Consequences stay the size of the mistake. Privacy is not lying, truth doesn't automatically fix things, and nobody has to confess, apologize or forgive.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A child asks a villager to judge whose sand turtle is better: find something true to say about each, or ask what they think.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) and (child), a friend, have each drawn a turtle in the wet sand, and (friend) has run to fetch (subject) to judge. "Which one is better?" (subject) looks. (child)'s turtle is very good. (friend)'s turtle has nine legs.

choices.label: Find Something True to Say About Each

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "That one has the best shell I've ever seen," says (subject), about (child)'s. "And that one," about (friend)'s, "is the fastest turtle on Isola. Look at all those legs." Both children seem satisfied. (friend) adds a tenth leg, for extra speed.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Which do you think is better?" (friend) looks at both turtles for a long time. "That one has the right number of legs," (friend.he/she) admits. "But mine's going somewhere." (subject) agrees that this is important. So does (child). They both draw more turtles until the tide comes in and takes them all.
